product.name: Blink
product.one_liner: Anonymous ephemeral file sharing with minute-scale auto-delete, QR links, and privacy modes
product.audience: Android users who need a quick private file drop without accounts or permanent cloud copies

assumptions: Goal inferred as earn because AdMob units, rewarded Top Up, and a live Play listing with Contains ads are shipped
Primary audience is English-speaking Android users who already understand link-based file sharing
Creator can collect AdMob revenue in their region (Play listing lists Nepal support contact)
No Play Console or analytics export was available; install/rating metrics are omitted rather than guessed

coverage.notes: Reviewed Flutter lib entry, ads/consent/credits/encryption, theme, manifest, onboarding, history empty state, README, release notes, branding screenshots, Play listing, Blink-site privacy page. Did not run the app, review Worker backend source, iOS (none), or Play Console exports. No crash reporter package found in pubspec.

competitors.name: 1time.io
competitors.why_relevant: Browser one-time encrypted download links marketed as a Firefox Send / WeTransfer alternative

competitors.name: Privyfile
competitors.why_relevant: No-account private file links with optional E2E, timers, and one-time links

competitors.name: Transient Files
competitors.why_relevant: Temporary and one-time file links up to 1GB, no sign-up, QR/share

competitors.name: Smash
competitors.why_relevant: Popular temporary large-file transfer with link sharing; longer retention than Blink minute timers

categories.summary: Clear JTBD: send a file that dies, without an account
categories.why: Play listing and README both sell anonymous share with auto-delete. Code implements minute timers, Privacy Mode, Instant burn, and no-login credits. That maps to a real job people still use WeTransfer-class tools for, with a sharper privacy promise.
categories.why_not_higher: No user interviews, review quotes, or Console churn data proving switch intent from named tools. +2 needs primary evidence that people open Blink for this job weekly.

evidence.quote: Send a file. It disappears. No one else ever sees it.
Share files that vanish in minutes. No Accounts: Anonymous sharing

categories.summary: Mobile privacy modes + minute timers are a real wedge; web one-time tools still dominate the category story
categories.why: Versus 1time, Privyfile, Transient, and Smash, Blink ships a native Android flow with Privacy Mode / Instant burn, EXIF strip, QR, and 1-10 minute expiry. That is sharper than generic temporary transfer. The core job (encrypted link that dies) is still crowded on the web.
categories.why_not_higher: Needs a harder exclusive wedge that web tools cannot match (e.g. measured screenshot-block reliability, contactless share UX, or proven trust brand) plus store copy that names the contrast.

evidence.quote: Privacy Mode - Content available until timer expires
Exclusive share modes: Privacy or Instant burn
Privacy mode - screenshot protection

categories.summary: Rewarded MB + banner + app-open is implemented; unit economics and paid ceiling are unproven
categories.why: AdConfig defines rewarded MB (+25), timer extension, banner, and app-open units with maxDailyRewardedAds=4. CreditService syncs MB to a Worker. UMP consent exists. Model fits a free anonymous tool. No IAP/subscription path found, and app-open on cold start remains a policy and UX tax.
categories.why_not_higher: Ship a collectible paid Top Up or remove/heavily gate app-open, then show labeled revenue ceiling with real eCPM or Play earnings. No reliable eCPM benchmark available from inputs.

categories.summary: Consistent dark purple system; looks shipped, still familiar indie-glow territory
categories.why: AppTheme defines a single accent (#7c3aed), Inter + Poppins, glass cards, and clear hierarchy. Screenshots show one primary Share CTA, readable white-on-dark body, and coherent upload/QR/receive cards. Brand mark is distinctive. The purple-glow dark look is common for privacy apps, so distinctiveness is moderate.
categories.why_not_higher: Tighten uniqueness (less generic purple glow), verify AA on secondary grey labels across all screens, and keep ads visually separated from primary actions.

categories.summary: Fast path to share; onboarding and empty states exist; cold-start ads still interrupt
categories.why: Home makes upload the center. Confirm screen exposes timer chips and Privacy Mode before Share. Success shows QR + countdown. Three-page onboarding; history has empty copy. App Open is skipped during first onboarding session and delayed 2s, which is careful, but returning users still risk a full-screen ad before the next share.
categories.why_not_higher: Kill or further suppress app-open around share intents / mid-transfer, and prove offline and receive-error recovery with screenshots or measured drop-off.

categories.summary: Ephemeral by design; return loops are weak beyond daily quota and history
categories.why: Files vanish in minutes, so the product fights classic habit retention. History, default timer prefs, and daily 100MB credits give a light reason to reopen, but there is no durable personal corpus, social graph, or scheduled need. That is honest for the category, and still a growth risk if earn depends on DAU.
categories.why_not_higher: Add a non-creepy return reason (saved recipients/folders of links, widgets for remaining MB, or clear share-from-other-apps habit) and measure D1/D7 from Console.

evidence.quote: Auto-Expiry: Files vanish after 1-10 minutes
100 / 100 MB; 100 MB free daily
Server-managed MB credits; local prefs write-through cache

categories.summary: Live listing + QR/link/share intents are real distribution; no Console proof of traction
categories.why: Play listing is live with ads disclosure. Manifest registers SEND, SEND_MULTIPLE, and App Links to blink.darkmintis.workers.dev/b/. Success UX pushes QR. Marketing site and privacy page exist. Without installs, conversion, or ASO keyword evidence, growth quality stays inferred from surfaces, not results.
categories.why_not_higher: Provide Play Console acquisition/store-listing conversion and a focused ASO pass; add one intentional invite or receive-to-install loop with measurement.

categories.summary: Strong feature-first Flutter + real encryption tests; ops observability thin
categories.why: 187 Dart lib files under feature folders; README encodes architecture rules. AES-256-GCM with checksum layout; encryption and upload services have unit tests (~45 test files). Foreground service for transfers; cleartextTraffic false. No Sentry/Crashlytics/Firebase Crashlytics in pubspec, so production crash signal is weak.
categories.why_not_higher: Add crash reporting + breadcrumb coverage on upload/receive, and keep analyze/test green as release gates with evidence in CI.

evidence.quote: AES-256-GCM for authenticated encryption
cryptography, google_mobile_ads, flutter_foreground_task; no crashlytics
Critical paths must stay covered: encryption, upload/link flow, receive flow

categories.summary: E2E encryption, UMP, and a privacy page are real; consent fail-open and device IDs need honesty
categories.why: Encryption is client-side AES-GCM. Manifest disables cleartext. ConsentService uses UMP and can open privacy options. Blink-site ships privacy.html. Play Data safety discloses device or other IDs shared with third parties (ads). CreditService sends X-Blink-Device-Id. Consent catch path returns true (ads allowed), which is a compliance sharpness issue.
categories.why_not_higher: Fail closed (or non-personalized only) when UMP errors; document device-id purpose in-app; keep Data safety and policy text synced with rewarded/app-open behavior.

evidence.quote: On error, assume non-EU and allow ads (graceful degradation)
usesCleartextTraffic=false; networkSecurityConfig set
Device or other IDs may be shared with third parties; encrypted in transit
Privacy Policy for Blink - Ephemeral File Sharing

verdict_line: Sharp privacy utility with real encryption and a live store presence, held back by cold-start ads, thin return loops, and no crash pipeline.

findings.title: App Open ads still fire on returning cold starts
findings.why: After onboarding, main.dart delays 2 seconds then loads App Open. That protects first session, but every later cold start can cover the share surface users came for. For an ephemeral utility, that tax hits exactly when intent is highest.
findings.counterpoint: App Open is a common AdMob pattern and is suppressed during onboarding and via suppressShow during transfers.

evidence.quote: if (!allowAppOpen) return; delay 2s; loadAndShowAppOpenAd
App Open ad (shown on cold start)

findings.fix: Show App Open only after a completed share or on a long session gap; never when a SEND intent or deep link is pending.

findings.title: Product deletes the reason to return
findings.why: Minute-scale expiry is the brand. History and daily MB are light hooks. Earn models that need daily opens will struggle without a deliberate, privacy-safe return loop.
findings.counterpoint: Many file-transfer tools are intentional infrequent-use utilities; retention may matter less than share completion rate.

evidence.quote: Auto-Expiry: Files vanish after 1-10 minutes
100 MB free daily

findings.fix: Pick one return mechanic that does not store file contents (MB widget, last-share resume, or share-sheet education) and track D1/D7.

findings.title: No crash reporting package in the shipped app
findings.why: pubspec has ads, encryption, foreground tasks, and webviews, but no Crashlytics/Sentry. Live Android apps with background transfers will fail silently for most users.
findings.counterpoint: Ferret/Mole help local debugging; they are not a production crash pipeline.

evidence.quote: google_mobile_ads present; no firebase_crashlytics or sentry
Ferret.install(); Mole.install(enableInRelease: false)

findings.fix: Add a crash reporter with upload/receive breadcrumbs and a release blocker on new crash-free regressions.

findings.title: UMP errors fail open to personalized ads
findings.why: ConsentService.checkAndRequestConsent catches errors and returns true, allowing ads. That is convenient and weak for GDPR sharpness when the form path fails.
findings.counterpoint: Non-EU users may never see a form; failing open keeps UX working when Google UMP is flaky.

evidence.quote: On error, assume non-EU and allow ads (graceful degradation)

findings.fix: On UMP failure, initialize ads as non-personalized only (or delay ads) until status is known.

findings.title: Top Up is ad-only; no direct paid MB path
findings.why: README and UI sell Top Up via rewarded ads. CreditService is MB/adsToday. Users who hate ads have no clean pay escape, which caps ARPU and can raise frustration on a privacy-branded app.
findings.counterpoint: Anonymous no-login products often avoid Play Billing identity friction on purpose.

evidence.quote: Bonus: Watch ads for +25 MB
Top Up button beside quota

findings.fix: Add a small Play Billing MB pack or ad-free day pass if billing is available; otherwise rename Top Up so it does not imply purchase.

findings.title: Banner sits on the receive completion surface
findings.why: ss5 shows a banner under the Done CTA on a success/receive screen. Even if policy-legal, it competes with the one job of that screen.
findings.counterpoint: Anchored banners are standard; rewarded ads are the heavier lift for quota.

evidence.quote: Test Ad banner beneath Done

findings.fix: Keep banners on Settings/History, not on QR success or receive Done screens.

findings.title: No Play Console export in this review
findings.why: Distribution surfaces look good, but installs, store conversion, and ratings were not evidenced from Console. Growth score cannot honestly rise without them.
findings.counterpoint: Public listing proves the app is shipped; metrics can arrive in v2.

evidence.quote: Listing readable; no installs/rating figures captured in review inputs

findings.fix: Drop a Play Console overview CSV into MasterG/inputs for v2.

calibration_note: First review mean of verified scores is about 6.2 (range 4-7), intentionally below the >7 warning. Retention scored 4 because ephemerality fights DAU by design. Revenue kept at 5 despite solid AdMob plumbing because app-open tax and missing paid path limit earn credibility. No Play Console metrics; growth/revenue confidence capped at medium where comps exist but economics do not.
